lab_title: Structural Anatomy of the Human Heart and Pulmonary/Systemic Circulation
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers and four major valves of the heart
Trace the path of blood through the pulmonary and systemic circulation loops
Explain the structural differences between the right and left ventricles and their functional significance
Understand the role of cardiac valves in preventing backflow during the cardiac cycle

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the gross anatomy of the heart in anterior view and label the four chambers with color-coded highlights.
key_visuals: Anterior view of a human heart in neutral position
Right atrium highlighted in light blue
Right ventricle highlighted in darker blue
Left atrium highlighted in light red
Left ventricle highlighted in darker red
Faint outline of ribs and thorax for context
student_actions: Rotate and inspect the 3D heart model from multiple angles
Tap on each chamber to reveal its name and basic function
Observe and note the relative size differences between chambers, especially the thicker wall of the left ventricle

scenes.brief_purpose: Zoom in on each of the four valves, showing their anatomical position and basic structure (leaflets/cusps).
key_visuals: Tricuspid valve between right atrium and right ventricle with three cusps visible
Pulmonary valve at the entrance to the pulmonary artery with three semilunar cusps
Mitral (bicuspid) valve between left atrium and left ventricle with two cusps visible
Aortic valve at the entrance to the aorta with three semilunar cusps
Chordae tendinae and papillary muscles visible at atrioventricular valves
student_actions: Sequentially select each valve to highlight it and read its name and location
Observe the structural differences between atrioventricular valves (tricuspid and mitral) and semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic)
Rotate the heart to see how valves are positioned relative to chambers

scenes.scene_name: Major Vessels: Entry and Exit Points
scenes.brief_purpose: Label and identify the six major blood vessels that connect the heart to systemic and pulmonary circulation.
key_visuals: Superior vena cava entering the right atrium from above
Inferior vena cava entering the right atrium from below
Pulmonary arteries branching from the right ventricle toward the lungs
Pulmonary veins (left and right pairs) entering the left atrium
Aorta exiting the left ventricle and arching upward
Color-coding: deoxygenated blood in blue tones, oxygenated blood in red tones
student_actions: Tap on each major vessel to identify it and learn whether blood entering it is oxygenated or deoxygenated
Trace the path of a single blood vessel with a guided animation to show where it goes
Answer a quick question: which vessels carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs and which carry oxygenated blood from the lungs

scenes.scene_name: Right Side of the Circulation Loop: Deoxygenated Blood Route
scenes.brief_purpose: Animate the path of deoxygenated blood from the body through the right heart chambers to the lungs.
key_visuals: Deoxygenated blood (blue) flowing from vena cava into right atrium
Blood passing through tricuspid valve into right ventricle
Right ventricle contracting and pushing blood through pulmonary valve
Blood flowing into pulmonary arteries toward lungs (shown faintly in background)
Sequential highlighting of right atrium → tricuspid valve → right ventricle → pulmonary valve → pulmonary arteries
student_actions: Watch an animated sequence showing deoxygenated blood entering and exiting the right side of the heart
Pause the animation at three key points (atrium, ventricle, pulmonary valve) and identify each structure
Note the relatively thin myocardium of the right ventricle and consider why it needs less force

scenes.scene_name: Left Side of the Circulation Loop: Oxygenated Blood Route
scenes.brief_purpose: Animate the path of oxygenated blood returning from the lungs through the left heart chambers to the body.
key_visuals: Oxygenated blood (red) flowing from pulmonary veins into left atrium
Blood passing through mitral valve into left ventricle
Left ventricle contracting with visibly thicker myocardium and pushing blood through aortic valve
Blood flowing into aorta toward systemic circulation (shown branching upward and downward)
Sequential highlighting of pulmonary veins → left atrium → mitral valve → left ventricle → aortic valve → aorta
student_actions: Watch an animated sequence showing oxygenated blood returning from the lungs and exiting to the body
Pause the animation at three key points (atrium, ventricle, aortic valve) and identify each structure
Compare the thick myocardium of the left ventricle to the right and hypothesize why this difference exists

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the complete pulmonary and systemic circulation loops simultaneously, showing how the right and left sides work in parallel.
key_visuals: Two parallel animation loops: blue deoxygenated blood circulating through right heart and lungs, red oxygenated blood circulating through left heart and body
Color-coded pathways showing the pulmonary loop (heart → lungs → heart) and systemic loop (heart → body → heart)
The heart as the central pump driving both loops
Simplified representations of lungs and body tissues on the sides
student_actions: Observe the simultaneous animation of both circulation loops working together
Identify which loop serves the lungs and which serves the body
Note that both loops must be synchronized to maintain balance

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how each valve opens during the appropriate phase and closes to prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
key_visuals: Close-up views of each valve in open and closed positions
Tricuspid and mitral valves open during atrial contraction and ventricular filling, then close during ventricular contraction
Pulmonary and aortic valves closed during ventricular filling, open during ventricular contraction
Chordae tendinae under tension preventing prolapse of atrioventricular valves
Pressure gradients indicated with directional arrows showing why backflow is prevented
student_actions: Step through a cardiac cycle animation frame-by-frame, noting when each valve opens and closes
For each valve, identify what would happen if it failed to close properly (backflow scenario)
Answer a conceptual question about the sequence of valve opening and closing during one heartbeat

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the myocardial wall thickness of the right and left ventricles and explain the structural-functional relationship.
key_visuals: Cross-sectional view of both ventricles side by side
Right ventricle with visibly thinner myocardial wall
Left ventricle with visibly thicker myocardial wall (approximately 2.5–3 times thicker)
Labels indicating the systemic circulation requiring higher pressure and force
Simplified pressure values or force comparison between the two ventricles
student_actions: Measure or compare the wall thickness of each ventricle using the AR interface
Read a brief explanation of why the left ventricle must generate higher pressure than the right
Apply this understanding: predict the consequences of left ventricular hypertrophy in hypertension and discuss why the right ventricle would dilate in chronic pulmonary disease
